pages.title: Next GPU rental queue
pages.summary: Prepare offline and bundle required RTX 5090 work into one rental.
takeaways: Prepare both NTT builds, resident-chain timing, and CPU basis-conversion fixtures before renting.
On the 5090, run exactness and sanitizers first, then matched timings and profiling.

pages.title: Project & setup
pages.summary: Build the project and understand what has been tested.
takeaways: Build and run the CPU checks first; a GPU is optional for getting started.
The tested CUDA baseline works on the recorded Ada workload. The newer resident runtime still needs native GPU validation.

pages.title: NTT & butterflies
pages.summary: Learn why polynomial evaluation can be built from repeated butterflies.
takeaways: An NTT evaluates a polynomial at special points modulo a prime. Butterflies share work between those evaluations.
Start with the small examples, then follow the negacyclic form used by this project at N=65536.

pages.title: From CPU to CUDA
pages.summary: See how threads, blocks and shared memory execute the same transform.
takeaways: Threads compute independent butterfly pairs. A block keeps one group in shared memory across several stages.
At N=65536, columns handle far pairs and rows handle near pairs. Barriers and kernel order preserve the dependencies.

pages.title: 65536: work distribution
pages.summary: Trace one block and thread through the 65536-point forward and inverse NTT.
takeaways: View one tower as a 256×256 array. Columns own the first eight forward stages; rows own the last eight.
Try block 3 and thread 5 in the explorer. Inverse reverses the passes and scales by the modular inverse of N.

pages.title: CUDA buffers & dataflow
pages.summary: Follow inputs, device buffers and transfers through the synchronous CUDA wrapper.
takeaways: A tower stores one polynomial modulo one prime. At N=65536 it takes 512 KiB in the current uint64 format.
Fused multiplication uploads two inputs and downloads one result. Separate public calls repeat transfers between operations.

pages.title: Arithmetic bounds & tests
pages.summary: Understand safe integer ranges and the tests that check exact arithmetic.
takeaways: Canonical means a value from 0 to q−1. Each current butterfly keeps that range.
A 60-bit value fits in uint64_t, but its product needs a wider temporary. Independent bigint checks test these operations.

pages.title: OpenFHE representation
pages.summary: Match OpenFHE primes, roots, array positions and format labels.
takeaways: OpenFHE stores one prime-modulus array per tower. Copy them in their original order, with their exact roots.
Forward changes coefficients to bit-reversed evaluations. Changing a format label alone does not convert the values.

pages.title: Hybrid operation graph
pages.summary: Follow digit extension, key products and reduction in pinned OpenFHE code.
takeaways: Hybrid key switching extends digit arrays from Q to QP, accumulates two key products, then reduces them to Q.
The order and integer representatives matter. This page has exact CPU comparisons; GPU key switching is still future work.

pages.title: Device backend contract
pages.summary: Specify what a GPU handle, dependency and buffer owner must preserve.
takeaways: A GPU polynomial needs its primes, format, array order, owner and readiness—not only a pointer.
This is the full design proposal. The separate resident prototype implements a bounded subset; the cache and OpenFHE adapter remain planned.

pages.title: Resident operation chain
pages.summary: Compose NTT operations without downloading their intermediate arrays.
takeaways: Upload two inputs, run forward transforms and pointwise multiplication, then inverse-transform and download the result.
The runtime owns queued resources and preserves inputs. Host tests and CUDA compilation pass; native GPU execution of this new path is pending.

pages.title: Run & debug
pages.summary: Run a small CPU example and inspect one butterfly at a time.
takeaways: The N=8 example prints coefficients, evaluations and a recovered input. No CUDA device is needed.
Use a terminal on any supported CPU platform, or follow the supplied macOS VS Code debugger setup.

pages.title: GPU NTT implementations
pages.summary: Compare published GPU NTT techniques and choose experiments to measure.
takeaways: Study integer reduction, coalesced memory access, register staging and keeping data on the device.
Published techniques suggest experiments. They do not establish a speedup for this implementation.

pages.title: Choosing the GPU
pages.summary: Choose hardware using modular arithmetic, memory and complete-workload measurements.
takeaways: RTX 5090 is the primary target and RTX 4090 the planned control. Larger cards need a measured capacity or performance reason.
Peak bandwidth and Tensor throughput cannot predict this exact integer workload. Compare matched operations on named hardware.

pages.title: GPU rental market
pages.summary: Compare dated rental rates, whole-session costs and profiling requirements.
takeaways: The November 13 snapshot favors comparing a suitable RunPod RTX 5090 with a verified Vast.ai offer. Recheck the live quote.
Confirm tools and profiler permissions, include storage and setup time, then export the complete evidence before ending billing.

pages.title: Integration roadmap
pages.summary: Track completed evidence, the current native gate and later integration phases.
takeaways: The order is NTT → base conversion → Hybrid key switching → OpenFHE. Working-day labels are milestones, not calendar dates.
D11/P2 remains open: the temporary Ada baseline is measured, while primary RTX 5090 and remaining runtime/profiling acceptance are pending.

pages.title: Architecture decision
pages.summary: Read the accepted ownership, integration and failure-handling rules.
takeaways: Keep inputs immutable, return fresh results and retain resources until queued work has safely finished.
The proposed OpenFHE adapter replaces its host object only after success. CPU fallback is an explicit choice before GPU submission.

pages.title: Implementation backlog
pages.summary: Choose the next task and its observable acceptance checks.
takeaways: Verify the native baseline, then build resident NTT, conversion, key switching and the adapter in dependency order.
Each task records evidence and a completion criterion. Host preparation alone does not complete a native GPU milestone.

pages.title: Before renting a GPU
pages.summary: Prepare dependencies locally, then run the current native checks on a GPU.
takeaways: Use CPU time for builds and host checks. Spend rental time on the actual device, exactness, sanitizers and measurements.
Older Ada results apply to their recorded source. Run the current checks, including the new resident chain, before accepting new timings.

pages.title: Benchmarks & tuning
pages.summary: Design fair comparisons before changing kernels or publishing speedups.
takeaways: Match inputs, widths, tower counts and hardware. Separate setup, public-call, device-event and CPU timing boundaries.
Tune one major cost at a time, then accept a variant only with exact results and complete-workload measurements.

pages.title: First GPU run: analysis
pages.summary: Audit the first diagnostic run and understand its limited timing sample.
takeaways: The first Ada run passed its selected native checks and saved one averaged 46-bit timing row.
That row cannot isolate kernels, transfers or variability. The later full-matrix report adds raw samples and a separate OpenFHE CPU baseline.

pages.title: Full GPU matrix: analysis
pages.summary: Read the measured Ada baseline and the limits of its GPU/CPU comparison.
takeaways: Fused multiplication was faster than the unfused public chain in all 140 workloads, with a 2.36× median ratio.
Device-event time excludes uploads/downloads. The separate M1 CPU and temporary GPU results are not RTX 5090 or end-to-end CKKS measurements.

pages.title: Offline test tooling
pages.summary: Run separate GPU and CPU collections with validated samples and safe resume.
takeaways: Use GPU-only measurements on the rental and collect the OpenFHE CPU timings locally with matching parameters.
The collector keeps raw samples, provenance and failures. Resume reuses only matching, hash-checked records and reruns the required gates.

pages.title: Writing & publishing
pages.summary: Edit source, check the notebook and export it to the personal website.
takeaways: Write the purpose and result first; define unfamiliar terms and keep long evidence in labelled notes.
Build, validate links and inspect desktop/phone pages before exporting. A source push alone does not publish the personal website.
